newsitem.title: USA: NYC plans to recommend Brown & Wood for new agency.
newsitem.headline: NYC plans to recommend Brown & Wood for new agency.

text.p: New York City said Thursday it planned to recommend Brown & Wood LLP as the bond counsel for its new borrowing agency.
The appointment, which was approved by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and City Comptroller Alan Hevesi, still must be acted upon by the board of the New York City Transitional Finance Authority.
The agency, in a prepared statement, said the Authority staff planned to recommend to the underwriters that one of three firms be picked, on a deal-by-deal basis, to serve as underwriters' counsel.
The three law firms were Hawkins, Delafield & Wood, Rogers & Wells and Williams & Harris, and these recommendations also were approved by the mayor and city comptroller.
Rogers & Wells will be used for the first bond sale, expected around August or September, and Lehman Brothers will be the lead underwriter.
